H91 road decolonization mission and permanent roadwarrior_decolonized modifier
Optional H91 settlement and Karashar Z57 boundary
H91 native national-idea names/descriptions; bounds are a locator envelope for separate sets

english_verification.review_scope: Representative current-Mod convoy, road-decolonization and settlement boundaries read; the fixed-revision English Roadwarrior Clan page was read as identity support only. It is a short page and does not certify a complete clan history, population losses or post-switch mechanics; no exhaustive mission or national-idea audit. Native English idea names/descriptions were compared by localisation key with the current Mod. Wide line ranges locate separately read passages, not exhaustive coverage. No formal validator, build, browser or gameplay test was run.

rationale.colonization: It favours destruction and migration over building colonies.
rationale.complexity: Migration, resources, overload and cooldowns must be managed.
rationale.dark_story: Scorched earth, harm to residents and making areas uninhabitable have explicit evidence.
rationale.difficulty: Mistakes can leave the mobile country unable to recover; no hands-on playtest was performed.
rationale.diplomacy: Diplomacy is not the mission line's focus.
rationale.early_pressure: The initial warband must open a route quickly.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Modifications and war technology exist, but this is not a high-magic story.
rationale.narrative_density: Convoy upgrades and scorched earth form a continuous narrative.
rationale.tall_play: Stable development conflicts with the convoy mechanics.
rationale.trade_economy: Loot and supplies matter more than conventional trade.
rationale.warfare: Progress depends mainly on fighting and raiding.

identity.appearance: A Black Orc warband existing in 1444.
identity.formation_scope: H91 is itself a starting country; after meeting separate settlement conditions it may choose to form Karashar Z57, which is not automatically inherited from this mission tree.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
Maxug's premonition of becoming the first "Roadwarrior" was compiled into a series of scattered journals, gathered by the Roadcult Book-Engineers in their journey across the Dwarovrod. It detailed Maxug's dreams to devastate the entire Dwarovar, raiding from hold to hold and claiming the many treasures still left by the ancient dwarven empire.

Many orcs from around the Dwarovar joined Maxug’s cause for the promise of loot, but many in turn started to believe in his vision of expanding the great convoy.

description.text:
The Cult of the Road reveres the Dwarovrod itself, seeing it as their domain that they took from the dwarves. With this, they believe that squatters on the roads violate their domain and that they must be stamped out. To maintain our power, new generations must be trained to revere and continue protecting our sacred road.

In our travels, we have discovered many insights on the road as our shamans received visions on its secrets and the many rituals needed to ensure our victory against any intruders daring to defile the holy road.

description.text:
On the great road we find many enemies, from weak dwarven remnants to occasional giant cave trolls, but everyone we face must die fighting. This tradition is not to preserve our honour or the enemy’s, but rather for us to continue growing stronger, for great rivals have a beauty like none other, and our blades should be tempered with the blood of the strong.

Rather than showing an example to our younger generation which would grow weak fighting unarmed fleeing enemies, we temper their skills in the blood of worthy adversaries.

description.text:
After successful raids, the Roadwarriors would perform large celebrations in the ruins. Many orcs gathered to perform by beating their drums of war and mixing war chants with screams, emulating the screech of metal moving on rails. The festivals often went wild, with the drummers breaking their instruments on stage and throwing themselves off into the crowds.

The music at these festivals was dubbed "Rail Metal" and became very popular after the "artists" perfected their art more and more after successful raids.

description.text: The shamans of the Roadwarrior clan accidentally discovered that channelling lightning magic through the rails of the holy road managed to magically restore them. Using this information, the mages would learn ways to manipulate lightning magic for both offence and to restore broken segments. The most talented of mages managed to entrap enemies into cages made of pure chains of lightning, trapping both orcs and their prey to have a fair fight where no quarter would be given.

description.text: The orcs not fit to be warriors in the great convoy instead take the role of rail conductors, they navigate the ruins of the Great Road, thus allowing the warriors to reach holds quicker. They maintain the convoy, clear debris on tracks and occasionally scout, allowing our vanguard to easily travel towards new enemies. However, as the conductors do not fight, they take a lower cut of the plunder and are often seen as outcasts to the strongest warriors of the clan.

description.text:
Due to the constant state of war all across the Dwarovar, there were not many permanent settlements made by any of the inhabitants, apart from some remaining dwarven holds. Due to there being little to no unity across the many races, stragglers would often fight for the limited resources and camp in any cave that looked safe enough, but fear would overcome anyone who heard the drums of the Roadwarrior clan.

Booming and echoing across every crevice nearby caves, the drums made it sound as if their enemies were surrounded by the Roadwarriors. Many were overcome with dread and gave up attempts of escape, which ensured the lack of stray victims escaping with supplies, and less competition against the great convoy.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who want to build holds, keep stable territory and conduct conventional diplomacy.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Maintain convoy resources, raid and surge along the roads, and decide whether to remain mobile or settle after meeting the conditions.
player_overview.overview: Roadwarrior is the Black Orc warband of 1444. Its dedicated gameplay is not holding a mine or building a stable realm, but assembling a Great Convoy, migrating along underground roads, raiding, modifying vehicles and pressing forward; overload and supplies make timing each charge essential. Missions can leave sections of road unable to be normally colonized for a long time. This is a uniquely anti-development campaign, with a later turn toward Karashar remaining optional.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy extremely fast, high-risk and destructive warfare.
signature_features: The Great Convoy and one-province migration dominate the campaign tempo.
Vehicle upgrades, high-speed movement and cooldown management are interlinked.
Scorched-earth effects change later development rather than ordinary territorial expansion.
player_overview.tagline: Drive the underground Great Convoy, fight as you move, and leave scorched earth behind.

reasons: A rare underground war-convoy migration system.
A strong warfare tempo with route decisions.
warnings: It is unsuitable for cautious development play.
The destruction of areas crossed has long-term consequences.

positive_indicators: Warband members gain shared survival and organization through the convoy.
values.rationale: Explicit scorched earth and making areas uninhabitable harm residents and later livelihoods; no deduction is made merely for Orc identity, nomadism or ordinary war.
red_flags: Some roads are permanently prevented from being recolonized.
Event text describes the burning of habitable environments.
